narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 14 % chance you won’t pass your final year, which is above the 10 % threshold that triggers extra support. That’s why you’re being asked to take remedial courses—it’s not a punishment, but a safety net to help you stay on track.

Three things stood out in the prediction. First, the reason you chose this school actually worked in your favor. Many students pick a school because of its reputation, and that choice seems to have given you a small boost toward passing. Second, you’ve never failed a class before, which is a strong positive sign. Most students who pass also have a clean record, so this is one of your biggest strengths. Finally, you’ve said you want to go on to higher education, and that ambition is helping the model see you as more likely to succeed.

However, the model still sees enough risk to recommend extra help. You’re studying less than two hours a week, which is well below what most of your classmates report. You also spend a lot of time going out with friends and have very high weekend alcohol use compared to others. These habits can make it harder to keep up with schoolwork, even if you’re motivated.

The next step is simple: use the remedial courses to build a routine. Set aside a little more time each week for focused study, and try to balance your social life so it doesn’t interfere with your goals. You’ve got the drive and the track record—small adjustments can make a big difference.
